To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hadronic lightby- light contribution to the muonic anomalous magnetic moment a(mu) is positive, that the coefficient of the two-loop graphs with two anomalous vertices, which dominates this contribution, is positive, that this coefficient is enhanced by the presence of a light pseudoscalar, and that this enhancement leads to a sizable reduction, by about 20%, of the discrepancy between a(mu) measured in experiment and a(mu) computed within the standard model.

the hadronic lightby-light scattering contribution to a(mu) is dominated by the pion-poles, that the coefficient of the two-loop logarithm is positive, and that the pion-polar contribution is positive.
the leading logarithm from the two-loop diagrams involving two anomalous couplings is positive and that the corresponding coefficient is 0.0006(2).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hadronic light by light scattering contribution to the anomalous magnetic moments of the muon and the electron.
the calculation of the hadronic light by light contribution to the muonic magnetic moment.
the calculation of the hadronic light by light contribution to the muons g - 2 in the framework of the chiral perturbation theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hadronic light by light scattering contribution to the anomalous magnetic moments of leptons is still a subject of active research.
the present status of the hadronic light by light scattering is not as clear as one would have hoped, and that further theoretical and experimental progress is necessary to resolve the situation.
the present theoretical uncertainty of a(mu) is still too large to allow for a definite statement about the existence or absence of physics beyond the standard model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that, in an effective field theory framework, the leading logarithms arising from the two-pion loop graphs with two anomalous vertices are positive and large enough to reduce the discrepancy to an experimentally acceptable level.

the leading logarithms from the two-loop anomalous graphs are positive and sizable, and therefore they should be taken into account in the analysis of the hadronic lightby-light scattering contribution.

the hadronic light by light scattering correction to a(mu) has a sizable positive contribution from the two-loop diagrams involving two anomalous pion vertices, and that the discrepancy between the experimental value of a(m) and the standard model prediction can be explained by the contributions from the hadronic light scattering and the hadronic vacuum polarization corrections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hadronic lightby-light scattering contribution is likely to be much smaller than the present estimate based on the vector-meson-dominance model.
the leading logarithmic term in the two-loop graphs is positive, and that this term is the dominant contribution to the hadron light-by-light scattering correction.
the hadronic light by light contribution to muon g-2 is dominated by pion exchange, and is positive.
